dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: If you're not here to hitch a boat ride, there really isn't any reason to stay. How about sailing to the city?

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: That gentleman from Sumeru seems to be a real careful sort. He'll be fine even if I don't guide him, I reckon.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: Yes. He seems to work at the Akademiya, and decided to travel here during a vacation.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: I've heard that he's very meticulous in research and in life. He found me through several layers of relationships, and invited me to be his guide.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: Which is fine, of course. I've got lots of free time, so I can accompany him anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: But compared to traveling itself, he seems to enjoy designing itineraries more — he even wanted to carefully calculate the length of aquabus rides.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can help to speed him up.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: It's okay. I don't mean to rush him. It is a good thing to think carefully while making plans for the future and then slowly enjoying the rest of it.

dialogues.speaker: Cheriez
dialogues.text: It's just that he seems to be a bit too preoccupied and forgot to have some of the bread that I brought for him. I can't finish the bread alone. Would you like to share it with me?
